turns.text: Hey Lloyd, I'm trying to get QMD running on my new Mac. The build keeps failing with some architecture mismatch error.
Ah, that's a common issue with the transition to newer chips. Did you check if your Node version matches the architecture?
I thought it was universal, but it turns out QMD requires native arm64 Node on Apple Silicon. Once I reinstalled Node via arm64 homebrew, it compiled fine.
Got it. Using the native binaries is definitely the way to go there. Glad you got it sorted!
Yeah, finally. Also, did that package from Amazon arrive? I ordered some thermal paste.
I don't have access to your shipping notifications, but usually Amazon Prime delivers within two days. Did you check your tracking?
Just checked, it's out for delivery. Should be here by 5. Thanks for the help with the build.
You're welcome! Let me know if you hit any other snags.
Lloyd, I'm looking at the local LLM training workshop materials. Can we actually run those fine-tuning scripts on my laptop?
It depends on the framework and your hardware specs. Most modern frameworks have added support for unified memory architectures recently.
I checked the docs. It says Apple Silicon (MPS) is supported for local LLM training in the workshop. So I should be good to go.
That's great news. You'll likely see faster iteration times compared to CPU-only training.
Awesome. I'm also trying to decide what to make for dinner. Thinking maybe tacos?
Tacos are a solid choice. Do you have all the ingredients, or are you planning a quick grocery run?
I have the tortillas and meat, but I'm out of salsa. Maybe I'll just use some hot sauce.
Hot sauce works too. Enjoy your coding and your dinner!
